o1.biggest_strength: One clean recommendation, a $79 Agency plan, with revenue math that ties out to my numbers. It includes a break-even on Team move-downs, a customer email that shows each person's own current bill, and clear go and stop rules.
o1.biggest_mistake: It treats the yearly-billing gap as a footnote and never fixes the monthly default or offers yearly in-app. It also assumes half of Essentials 8+ customers switch and their churn drops to 5% without much support.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add a proper yearly-billing step, a faster win than the new plan. State plainly that the first two quarters come from churn reduction because of the 12-month price hold. Support the 50% switch and 5% churn assumptions with something firmer.

o2.biggest_strength: It uses all three signals in my data: the Essentials 8+ leak (374 customers, $23.9k a month), the yearly-billing gap, and the 12-month promise. It gives low, mid and high cases and says honestly that the low case is near zero and yearly won't help within two quarters. It has a dated plan and a measurable stop rule.
o2.biggest_mistake: $99 is about 55% above what an 11-channel Essentials customer pays now, so the 25% upgrade assumption looks optimistic. The 'bolder move' section edges toward a menu when I asked for one recommendation. It is dense and uses terms like MRR and holdout.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Price Agency closer to the current bill, or defend $99 with evidence. Drop or fold in the bolder-move section. Write in plainer words and keep a single recommendation, with the yearly change clearly secondary.

reason: Both recommend the right flat Agency plan for the Essentials 8+ group with sound math. Output 2 also uses the yearly-billing signal and the grandfathering limit, and gives an honest range of outcomes. Output 1 is cleaner, warmer and priced more realistically, but it treats yearly billing as an afterthought.
